collections.title: OSINT Methodology Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.description: Browse research on open-source intelligence methods: collecting, validating and connecting public information, with original publication details and source links.
collections.intro: Open-source intelligence (OSINT) turns publicly available information into material that can support an investigation. The methodological questions matter as much as the tools: how information was found, whether it can be verified, and what conclusions the available evidence can support.
collections.scope: This collection contains papers assigned to ALEX’s OSINT Methodology research category. It brings together work on information collection, validation, linkage and the organisation of investigative work. It is a subject collection, rather than a list of papers selected for one particular kind of investigation.
collections.use: Use the bibliography to compare collection approaches, examine validation methods and trace the research behind an investigative technique. Consult the original paper for its data, assumptions and limitations before applying a method. A classification in this collection does not establish that a tool is suitable for a particular case.
collections.summary: Collecting, validating and connecting public information for investigative work.

collections.title: Social Media & SOCMINT Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Public platform content, online communities and social-media intelligence methods.
collections.description: Browse social-media intelligence research on public posts, online communities and platform data, with bibliographic details and original source links.
collections.intro: Social-media intelligence examines information shared through online platforms and communities. Posts, accounts and interactions can provide investigative leads, but their meaning depends on platform context, collection conditions and the reliability of the material being observed.
collections.scope: The Social Media & SOCMINT category groups papers about social-platform information and its analysis. Subject matter can include public-post collection, community behaviour, information extraction and cyber-threat awareness. The separate Social Media Analysis investigation collection provides another route through application-oriented assignments.
collections.use: Compare how studies select accounts or posts, handle missing or deleted content and establish the context of an interaction. A public post, an account identity and the person operating it are separate evidential questions. Read the underlying study before interpreting a platform-derived indicator as a finding.

collections.title: Dark Web & Underground Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Research on underground forums, online markets and concealed services.
collections.description: Find research on dark-web services, underground forums and online markets, with original publication details and links to the recorded sources.
collections.intro: Research on underground online activity examines how forums, markets and concealed services are organised and observed. Investigators may use this literature to understand a setting, interpret terminology or evaluate the limitations of a collected dataset.
collections.scope: This subject bibliography follows the existing Dark Web & Underground category assignment. It includes research associated with online markets, underground communities and information collected from those environments. Dark Web Analysis is the separate investigation-type collection for papers assigned to that application.
collections.use: Check when and where observations were collected, how access was obtained and which parts of a community were visible. Platform closures, restricted membership and changing aliases can limit comparisons across datasets. Claims about an account or marketplace should be assessed against the study’s own evidence.

collections.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Threat information collection, interpretation, sharing and analytical context.
collections.description: Explore cyber threat intelligence research on collection, extraction, sharing and analytical context, with publication references and original source links.
collections.intro: Cyber threat intelligence connects observations about threats with the context needed to use them. Research in this area examines how information is collected, extracted, represented and shared, and how an analyst can assess its relevance to a particular question.
collections.scope: The bibliography contains papers assigned to Cyber Threat Intelligence in ALEX’s subject taxonomy. It spans intelligence-oriented information processing and analysis; assignment to this category is separate from a paper’s use in threat hunting, attribution or incident response.
collections.use: Use the references to examine an intelligence workflow or the assumptions behind an extracted indicator. Check the provenance, time period and validation of the underlying observations. Published research does not establish that a listed indicator remains current or that a reported association identifies the same actor in another case.

collections.title: Digital Forensics & Evidence Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Digital artefacts, forensic processes and the interpretation of evidence.
collections.description: Browse digital forensics and evidence research on artefacts, collection and interpretation, with original publication years, references and source links.
collections.intro: Digital forensics examines artefacts and the processes used to collect, preserve and interpret them. A research method can illuminate what an artefact may show while also exposing dependencies on the device, software version or circumstances in which it was produced.
collections.scope: This collection uses the Digital Forensics & Evidence research-category assignment. It brings together papers associated with digital artefacts, evidence processing and forensic methods. The Forensic Investigation collection groups papers by investigative application rather than by subject alone.
collections.use: Compare the steps needed to reproduce a method, the environment in which it was tested and the limits of the inference it supports. Preserve the distinction between an observed artefact and an interpretation of it. Consult applicable procedures and the original research before using a technique in casework.

collections.title: Malware & Exploits Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Malicious software, exploitation mechanisms and related technical artefacts.
collections.description: Find malware and exploit research on malicious software, technical behaviours and exploitation mechanisms, with bibliographic details and source links.
collections.intro: Malware and exploit research investigates malicious software and the mechanisms through which systems can be compromised. The literature can help explain a technical artefact or compare detection approaches, provided the tested environment and the available evidence are understood.
collections.scope: The Malware & Exploits subject category supplies the membership of this bibliography. Papers assigned here can concern malicious-code behaviour, exploit mechanisms or related detection research. Malware Analysis is a separate application-oriented collection and may contain papers assigned to other subjects.
collections.use: Read how samples were selected and labelled, which versions or architectures were tested and how findings were validated. A result from a sample set does not establish that every variant behaves the same way. Use the source paper to distinguish demonstrated behaviour from a proposed detection technique.

collections.title: Vulnerability Research Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Weakness discovery, characterisation and research into software vulnerabilities.
collections.description: Explore vulnerability research on discovering and characterising security weaknesses, with original publication information and links to recorded sources.
collections.intro: Vulnerability research examines how weaknesses are discovered, described and evaluated. Research questions may concern a particular failure mechanism, the information used to identify a weakness or the performance of a discovery method.
collections.scope: This bibliography includes papers carrying ALEX’s Vulnerability Research category. Its subject-based membership differs from Vulnerability Assessment, which groups papers assigned to an investigative application. An entry here is a research reference, not a statement that a currently deployed product is vulnerable.
collections.use: Check affected configurations, software versions, disclosure context and the evidence used to demonstrate a weakness. When comparing discovery methods, look at the evaluation corpus and the treatment of false positives. Consult current authoritative product information separately before drawing conclusions about a live system.

collections.title: Disinformation & Influence Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Information manipulation, influence activity and the study of online narratives.
collections.description: Browse research on disinformation, influence and online information manipulation, with publication details and links to original research sources.
collections.intro: Research on disinformation and influence examines how information is produced, circulated and interpreted, including attempts to manipulate an audience. An observed narrative, a pattern of coordination and evidence of an organiser’s intent require different kinds of support.
collections.scope: The collection follows the Disinformation & Influence subject assignment in the accepted corpus. Papers can address content analysis, information diffusion and approaches to identifying misleading material. Inclusion does not certify a particular claim, account or political interpretation as false or coordinated.
collections.use: Examine how a study defines its labels, chooses a reference standard and measures uncertainty. Language, collection dates and platform selection can affect the results. Keep content-level observations separate from conclusions about intent, coordination or who is responsible for an activity.

collections.title: Cybercrime & Fraud Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Online offending, deception, victimisation and the organisation of fraud.
collections.description: Find cybercrime and fraud research on online offending, deception and victimisation, with original bibliographic records and links to source publications.
collections.intro: Cybercrime and fraud research examines offending that involves digital systems, online deception and the people or organisations affected. It provides ways to frame investigative questions about a scheme, its participants and the evidence needed to understand it.
collections.scope: This subject collection contains papers assigned to Cybercrime & Fraud. Its scope is broader than one mechanism such as phishing and can include research on offending patterns, online markets, victimisation and fraud-related behaviour represented in the accepted corpus.
collections.use: Use the literature to compare explanations of a scheme and identify the evidence a study actually used. Distinguish reported victim experiences, observed transactions and inferred offender behaviour. Population estimates and findings from a particular platform or jurisdiction should be read within their stated sampling limits.

collections.title: Network & Infrastructure Security Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Communications systems, network protection and infrastructure security research.
collections.description: Browse network and infrastructure security research on communications, monitoring and system protection, with publication details and original source links.
collections.intro: Network and infrastructure security research studies the systems that carry communications and support digital services. Investigative interpretation depends on where an observation was made and what the monitoring system could see.
collections.scope: ALEX’s Network & Infrastructure Security category determines this bibliography. It groups subject-oriented work concerning communications, network monitoring and infrastructure protection. Network Investigation and Incident Response provide separate collections organised around investigative use.
collections.use: Check the topology, traffic source and observation point used in an evaluation. Encrypted, sampled or incomplete traffic can change what a result means. A reported detection rate or network association should be interpreted against the conditions and ground truth documented by the original study.

collections.title: IoT & CPS Security Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Security of connected devices and systems that interact with physical processes.
collections.description: Explore Internet of Things and cyber-physical systems security research, with publication references, recorded authors and links to original sources.
collections.intro: Internet of Things and cyber-physical systems research concerns connected devices and systems that interact with a physical environment. The relationship between a digital observation and a physical event depends on device behaviour, system design and the available records.
collections.scope: This bibliography uses the IoT & CPS Security research-category assignment. It can include device, network and detection research associated with these environments. The category does not establish that a method tested on one device or testbed applies to another operational setting.
collections.use: Compare device capabilities, firmware, communication protocols and testbed assumptions. Look for the distinction between simulated traffic and observations from operational systems. Use the original paper to understand what a method measures and which safety or environmental conditions constrained its evaluation.

collections.title: Privacy & Surveillance Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Personal information, observation practices and the consequences of data collection.
collections.description: Find privacy and surveillance research on personal information, observation and data collection, with original publication details and recorded source links.
collections.intro: Privacy and surveillance research examines how information about people is collected, connected and used, and what consequences those practices can have. It can help investigators recognise the exposure created by data collection and the limits of an inference about an individual.
collections.scope: Papers in this bibliography carry ALEX’s Privacy & Surveillance research-category assignment. The subject can intersect with social platforms, identification methods and information governance. The listing preserves those existing assignments without making a legal judgement about a particular investigative practice.
collections.use: Examine which people and data sources a study represents, what consent or access assumptions it makes and how it evaluates potential harm. Technical feasibility does not determine legal authority. Use appropriate current policy and legal guidance separately when planning the collection or use of personal information.

collections.title: AI/ML for Security Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods applied to security problems.
collections.description: Browse AI and machine-learning security research on detection, classification and analysis, with original bibliographic details and source publication links.
collections.intro: Artificial intelligence and machine-learning research applies computational models to security questions such as classification, detection and information extraction. A model’s output is meaningful only in relation to its training data, evaluation design and the question it was built to answer.
collections.scope: The AI/ML for Security subject assignment supplies this collection’s membership. Papers may be associated with different investigative applications, including threat hunting, phishing analysis and vulnerability assessment. Category membership does not endorse a model or establish readiness for operational use.
collections.use: Compare dataset provenance, train/test separation, class balance, error rates and evaluation dates. Consider whether the test conditions resemble the intended investigation. Treat model-generated text or labels as outputs requiring verification against source evidence rather than as independent evidence of an event.

collections.title: Foundations & Surveys Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Background research, reviews and overviews for framing a research question.
collections.description: Explore foundational and survey research in the ALEX library, with publication references and source links for tracing background literature and cited methods.
collections.intro: Foundational work and surveys can help a reader map a research area, understand terminology and identify earlier studies. Their value for an investigation depends on the question being asked and the period and literature that a review covers.
collections.scope: This bibliography follows ALEX’s Foundations & Surveys category assignment. It collects records classified as background or overview material rather than selecting papers for a single investigative application. Entries retain the scope and metadata recorded in the accepted library.
collections.use: Start with a review’s stated search strategy, inclusion criteria and publication cutoff. Follow references to primary studies when evaluating a technical or empirical claim. An overview can organise the literature without resolving disagreements between studies or establishing that older techniques remain applicable.

collections.title: Network Investigation Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Interpreting communications, traffic observations and network relationships.
collections.description: Browse research assigned to network investigation, with references relevant to communications, traffic observations and network relationships.
collections.intro: Network investigation uses observations of communications and relationships between systems to answer a defined question. The interpretation of an address, connection or traffic pattern depends on the collection point, time period and supporting context.
collections.scope: This collection contains papers assigned to the Network Investigation application. Their research categories can differ, because an investigative use is separate from a subject classification. The bibliography is a research starting point rather than a set of current network indicators.
collections.use: Compare what each method observes, how it establishes ground truth and what information is absent. Shared infrastructure and changes over time can complicate the meaning of an address-level association. Use the original study to assess which conclusions follow from the data it actually collected.

collections.title: Social Media Analysis Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Investigative analysis of platform content, accounts and interactions.
collections.description: Find research assigned to social media analysis, with references for examining public content, accounts, interactions and platform-derived evidence.
collections.intro: Social media analysis examines platform material in relation to an investigative question. Content, account behaviour and interaction patterns offer different observations, and each requires context before an analyst can infer a relationship or activity.
collections.scope: The bibliography follows the Social Media Analysis investigation-type assignment. It can draw on several research subjects, including social-media intelligence, information manipulation and machine learning. Subject collections remain available as a separate way to explore the same library.
collections.use: Look at collection boundaries, platform features, language and the way a study handles automated or missing activity. Verify original content where possible and separate an account-level observation from an assertion about a person. Evaluate coordination claims against the study’s definitions and supporting evidence.

collections.title: Dark Web Analysis Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Investigative work involving concealed services, underground markets and forums.
collections.description: Explore research assigned to dark web analysis, with references for understanding concealed services, underground markets and forum evidence.
collections.intro: Dark web analysis investigates material associated with concealed services and underground online environments. An analyst must account for how access, observation and changing platform conditions shape the evidence available to a study.
collections.scope: This application-oriented bibliography follows the Dark Web Analysis assignment. It includes records from different research categories; it is distinct from the Dark Web & Underground subject collection, even where membership overlaps.
collections.use: Examine the study’s access method, collection period and treatment of aliases, listings and transactions. A listing is not by itself evidence of a completed transaction, and observations from one community may not describe another. Trace conclusions back to the source data and the limitations reported by the authors.

collections.title: Malware Analysis Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Examining malicious-code artefacts and the behaviour they can support.
collections.description: Browse research assigned to malware analysis, with original publication references for examining malicious software, artefacts and technical behaviour.
collections.intro: Malware analysis examines software and related artefacts to understand their characteristics or behaviour. The evidence available from static inspection, execution observations and derived features can differ, so the analysis method needs to be explicit.
collections.scope: The Malware Analysis investigation-type assignment determines this collection’s membership. Papers can come from malware research, machine learning or other subjects in the accepted corpus. A research classification does not establish that a technique identifies every member of a malware family.
collections.use: Check sample provenance, lab conditions, labelling and the behaviour observable in the study’s environment. Compare the explanation of a finding with the evidence that supports it. When evaluating detection research, examine errors and sample selection as well as aggregate performance.

collections.title: Attribution Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Assessing relationships, responsibility and the strength of identity-related inferences.
collections.description: Find attribution research on linking observations, assessing relationships and evaluating identity-related inferences, with original bibliographic source links.
collections.intro: Attribution research examines how observations may be connected to accounts, systems, groups or people. These are different levels of inference: similarity, shared infrastructure and evidence of control do not necessarily answer the same question.
collections.scope: This bibliography includes papers assigned to the Attribution investigation type. Its membership spans the subject categories represented in ALEX. The presence of a paper in this collection is not an endorsement of a particular attribution claim or a statement about an actor’s responsibility.
collections.use: Use the references to examine alternative explanations, uncertainty and the evidence needed for each step in an inference. Check whether apparent links rely on independent sources or repeat the same observation. Report the level of confidence supported by the original evidence rather than extending an association beyond it.

collections.title: Phishing Analysis Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.description: Explore research classified for phishing analysis, including deceptive messages, URLs and websites, detection approaches and campaign evidence, with source links.
collections.intro: Phishing analysis examines deceptive messages, websites and supporting infrastructure to understand how an attempt works and how related activity might be recognised. Research can help investigators assess indicators and detection methods, while keeping the evidence behind a finding separate from a model’s prediction.
collections.scope: This bibliography contains papers assigned to ALEX’s Phishing Analysis investigation type. That assignment describes an investigative application; it is separate from the research category. Papers may therefore approach phishing through fraud research, machine learning, threat intelligence or other subjects represented in the accepted library.
collections.use: Use these references to investigate message and URL characteristics, compare detection approaches and find studies relevant to campaign analysis. Check the original study’s dataset, evaluation period and error rates: results from one dataset or period may not transfer to another investigation. These papers are research references, rather than a live feed of phishing indicators.
collections.summary: Research relevant to deceptive messages, websites, URLs and phishing campaigns.

collections.title: Forensic Investigation Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Investigative use of digital artefacts, preservation and evidence interpretation.
collections.description: Explore research assigned to forensic investigation, with original references for collecting, preserving, analysing and interpreting digital artefacts.
collections.intro: A forensic investigation uses digital artefacts to address questions about an event or activity. A reproducible process and a clear account of what the artefacts can show are central to interpreting a technical finding.
collections.scope: This application-oriented collection contains records with the Forensic Investigation assignment. Papers may belong to digital forensics, OSINT or other research subjects. It complements the Digital Forensics & Evidence subject bibliography while preserving the distinction between the two classification dimensions.
collections.use: Read how evidence was acquired and preserved, what processing changed its representation and which assumptions support the interpretation. Check tool, software and environment dependencies before attempting reproduction. The research listing provides references, not a determination of evidentiary admissibility or procedural suitability.

collections.title: Threat Hunting Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Research for forming and examining hypotheses about possible threat activity.
collections.description: Browse threat hunting research on investigative hypotheses, observations and detection approaches, with publication details and original source links.
collections.intro: Threat hunting starts with a question or hypothesis about possible threat activity and examines available observations for evidence. Research can inform how that question is framed, which signals are examined and how a result is validated.
collections.scope: This bibliography uses ALEX’s Threat Hunting investigation-type assignment. It draws on different subjects, including threat intelligence, network security and machine learning. Membership reflects the stored application classification rather than an assertion that a paper describes a complete operational hunting workflow.
collections.use: Compare the data a method requires, the time period it covers and the process used to verify a signal. Distinguish absence of an observation from evidence that an activity did not occur. Evaluate a proposed technique against the visibility and error costs of the investigation in which it might be used.

collections.title: Vulnerability Assessment Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Evaluating weaknesses, exposure and the evidence supporting an assessment.
collections.description: Find vulnerability assessment research on identifying weaknesses and evaluating exposure, with original publication details and recorded source links.
collections.intro: Vulnerability assessment evaluates weaknesses and their relevance to a defined system or context. The existence of a reported weakness, its applicability to a configuration and the consequences of exposure are related but separate questions.
collections.scope: This collection contains papers assigned to the Vulnerability Assessment investigation type. It can include methods from vulnerability research, network security and other subjects in the corpus. The references do not provide a current inventory of affected products or systems.
collections.use: Check the assessment’s scope, required access, configuration assumptions and evidence of an applicable weakness. Compare how methods treat false positives and incomplete coverage. Use current authoritative advisories separately when determining whether a research finding applies to a live environment.

collections.title: Incident Response Research | ALEX by RISE
collections.summary: Research for investigating, interpreting and responding to security incidents.
collections.description: Explore incident response research on security-event investigation, evidence interpretation and response processes, with original publication references.
collections.intro: Incident response brings investigation and action together when a security event needs to be understood and addressed. Research can help explain the information required for a decision and the effects that collection or response actions may have on later analysis.
collections.scope: The bibliography follows ALEX’s Incident Response investigation-type assignment. Its records can address different research subjects, from forensic evidence to threat intelligence and network observations. The collection is a set of research references rather than a substitute for an organisation’s incident procedures.
collections.use: Examine what was known when a decision was made, which evidence was preserved and how the study evaluates a response outcome. Separate technical observations from assumptions about an event’s cause or extent. Account for the environment and constraints described by the authors before transferring a proposed process to another setting.

bibliography.title: Complete Cybercrime & OSINT Bibliography | ALEX by RISE
bibliography.description: Browse the complete accepted ALEX research bibliography across all sources, including miscellaneous classifications, with publication details and source links.
bibliography.intro: This directory provides a publication-year route through every accepted record in ALEX. It includes all recorded research categories and investigation types, across all sources, so a paper remains discoverable even when it is assigned to Other or has no separate topic page.
bibliography.scope: The bibliography reproduces the complete accepted public corpus, ordered by original publication year as recorded and then by title. Each entry retains its existing assignments and available citation metadata. Miscellaneous classifications describe how a record is stored; they do not define a new research subject.
bibliography.use: Follow a paper’s title to its recorded DOI or source, or use its category and investigation-type links to explore a narrower collection. Missing citation details are identified rather than filled in. Use ALEX search for full abstracts and combined filters, and consult the original publication to verify a reference.
